reviewProvenance: Two findings supplied by the delegating owner's independent PR4239 review; no independent acceptance is claimed for this repair.

P1.problem: A failed cleanup remained eligible while its callback executed; reentrant retry/cancel could release the original holder and resolve settled before the outer callback threw.
P1.repair: Per-resource cleanupInProgress and cancellationInProgress guards block same-resource release/retry/cancel reentry. Cleanup retains the actual holder and closure until the outer callback returns successfully. trySettle requires finished invocation, settled local terminals, no callback in progress, no cleanup failure and no retained handle/cleanup/cancel closures.
P1.throwPath: The outer cleanup catch retains original holder/closure, marks unknown and appends the actual cause. finally clears only the in-progress flag; outstanding debt still prevents settlement.
P1.analogousBoundary: Cancellation callbacks also have a same-resource reentry guard and settlement barrier; they do not grant native completion or allow cleanup to release their holder while active.

P2.problem: observe checked cancellation before executing start, but reading options.quality inside start could abort the signal and still invoke encode/toBlob.
P2.repair: Prepare the actual request/quality and bind the same provider method before checking the original owner cancellation immediately before the invocation. Codec normalization explicitly bypasses the exact original cancellation reason; actual native codec errors retain their original metadata/cause.
